bug_semantics: CipAppPath::deserialize_symbolic trusts a symbolic-segment header's self-declared length and copies that many bytes from the current input pointer without checking remaining readable size. CipMessageRouterRequest::DeserializeMRReq (and historically InitRequest) only validates the outer path word-count (path_size = word_count*2) and then hands a 2-byte BufReader/limit to the app-path parser. A remote unconnected SendRRData Message Router request with body 0e 01 7f 41 therefore passes the outer check (path word count 1 → 2 path bytes 7f 41) while first=0x7f yields symbol_size=31; after consuming the header only 1 byte remains and memcpy/pointer-walk reads past the path window into/beyond the global TCP receive buffer s_buf. The same unbounded copy exists on the ANSI Extended Symbol branch. Demonstrated impact is a remotely triggerable out-of-bounds read / ASan global-buffer-overflow DoS on the official POSIX sample (CWE-125/CWE-119).
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism was first written in 186ffccd18abdcaa255f1fcb42a1a57bd920e538 (2016-10-19) when CipAppPath::deserialize_symbolic was added to source/src/cip/cipepath.c. The new symbolic-segment branch did `int symbol_size = first & 0x1f;` then `while( i < symbol_size ) tag[i++] = *p++;` with no `p < aLimit` check (and the ANSI Extended Symbol branch likewise copied `byte_count` bytes without remaining-limit checks). Parent 2d6b8f3eaafde2e6090cf76966b3d338f7e2b4f6 had only logical-segment DeserializePadded and no symbolic parser. 491dddf6b34ec66f01b6e1f4c2be248bca1568fe (2016-11-21) is a later BufReader refactor that replaced the while-loop with `memcpy( tag, in.data(), symbol_size )` while still bypassing BufReader bounds; that is a rewrite of the same first-written copy, not a new BIC. The sink stayed that memcpy until 886a4d090e1c5b0475f0b1c2fe0606a8f0d6a519 switched it to bounds-checked BufReader::get_bytes().
